entries.rationale: os.system(cmd) passes the entire command string through the shell (/bin/sh -c): full shell metacharacter interpretation with no quoting, i.e. the CWE-78 dangerous argument position (arg 0). cmd is caller-built: check() joins CLI-supplied file/directory names (args_str = ' '.join(args2), line 31) and interpolates them unquoted into run(f"ruff {args_str}") and run(f"flake8 {args_str}") (lines 33-34); the only prior filter is Path(arg).exists() (lines 25-29), an existence check that performs no command sanitization - an existing attacker-named file (e.g. a name containing ';' or '$(...)') still passes and is shell-interpreted. Repository-wide grep of the DB snapshot confirms this is the only command-execution call in the database.

entries.rationale: SUPPLEMENTARY entry (extraction gap - not a CSV row; flagged for reviewer attention). check(args: list[str]) is the sole external input boundary of this Typer CLI: @app.command() (line 21) makes it the 'adt check <names>' handler, and Typer injects the CLI-provided file/directory names into the args parameter. Those values demonstrably reach the os.system command string via ' '.join(args2) (line 31) and the f-strings at lines 33-34 -> run() -> os.system (line 16). Added for Phase 2 recall; without it the pass has no source at all because sources.csv is empty (Call-shaped decorators never matched sources.ql's isTyperHandler). Threat model: the boundary is the local CLI user - attacker-relevant when adt is invoked on untrusted names (e.g. attacker-created filenames inside a checked-out repository that pass the Path.exists() filter while carrying shell metacharacters).
